article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 50% Indica / 50% Sativa
Genetics: Sherb Cake × Super Buff Cherry #26
Breeder: Grow More Fire Genetics
THC Content: 22–28%
CBD Content: Typically low, generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , limonene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Sweet cherry, creamy berry, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to early October
Indoor Yield: 450–550 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 500–700 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Royal Cake occupies an interesting place among modern dessert cannabis strains because its name suggests something heavy, sugary, and traditional while its genetics point in a considerably brighter direction. Rather than simply stacking another Kush or Cookies line onto Wedding Cake , Grow More Fire Genetics combined the creamy, fruity character of Sherb Cake with its intensely colorful Super Buff Cherry #26 selection.

The result is a balanced marijuana hybrid built around contrasting qualities: dense resinous flowers paired with vivid fruit terpenes, an initially lively head change followed by physical ease, and sweet bakery notes threaded with tart cherry and citrus. Grow More Fire lists the cultivar as a 50/50 hybrid with a flowering time of roughly 60 days, making this specific version distinct from unrelated cannabis products that occasionally appear under the same Royal Cake name.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder identifies Royal Cake as Sherb Cake × Super Buff Cherry #26. In this cross, the Sherb Cake parent is the Seed Junky Genetics selection described by Grow More Fire as Girl Scout Cookies × Pink Panties . That side of the family supplies much of the creamy sherbet, sweet berry, doughy spice, and dense flower structure associated with the plant. It also brings substantial Cookies influence into the pedigree, which helps explain why some phenotypes develop a rich confectionery aroma despite the strong fruit character coming from the other side of the cross.

Super Buff Cherry #26 contributes a much more elaborate family tree. Grow More Fire created the #26 keeper by combining the Blockberry/ Super Boof cut—derived from Black Cherry Punch and Tropicana Cookies —with Relentless Genetics’ Tropicana Cherry, itself descended from Tropicana Cookies and Cherry Cookies F3. That means Royal Cake carries a heavy concentration of cherry, citrus, Cookies, and Tropicana genetics underneath its dessert-style exterior. The breeder specifically selected Super Buff Cherry #26 as a keeper, and its lineage helps account for the offspring’s potential purple coloration, resin coverage, fruit intensity, and vigorous hybrid growth.

Because Royal Cake was released as feminized seed rather than a single clone-only selection, some variation should be expected from plant to plant. One phenotype may lean toward Sherb Cake with creamier berry and vanilla tones, while another may emphasize orange zest, ripe cherry, tropical fruit, and sharper candy aromas inherited through Super Buff Cherry. Grow More Fire describes the cross as capable of attractive coloration and possible Sherb-dominant terpenes rather than claiming every seed will produce an identical expression.
Effects and Experience

Royal Cake’s balanced genetic makeup tends to create a more layered experience than the sleepy name might imply. The opening phase can feel mentally buoyant, with mood elevation, heightened interest in surroundings, easier conversation, and a gentle increase in sensory awareness. Music and food may become more engaging, and mundane activities can take on a more enjoyable quality. This cerebral lift generally lacks the sharp, racing quality associated with very stimulating sativas, although high doses may still feel intense for people with limited THC tolerance.

As the session develops, the body component becomes increasingly apparent. Muscles may feel looser, physical tension recedes, and the initial mental brightness settles into a calm, comfortable state. Moderate amounts can therefore fit relaxed social situations, movies, gaming, music, or an unhurried evening at home. Larger servings are more likely to shift the balance toward heaviness, reduced motivation, strong appetite, and a desire to remain seated.

Potency should not be underestimated. Neither Grow More Fire nor its current Royal Cake seed listing publishes an official THC percentage, so exact numbers depend on phenotype, cultivation, harvest timing, and laboratory testing. Its parentage, however, includes modern high-potency cannabis lines, with Super Buff Cherry selections commonly testing in the mid-20% THC range. Newer consumers should therefore approach slowly. Dry mouth and dry eyes are the most predictable unwanted effects, while excessive consumption may cause dizziness, mental fog, or temporary anxiety.
Medical Benefits

Medical marijuana consumers may find the cultivar’s combination of cerebral uplift and physical relaxation useful when they are looking for broad evening relief without immediately becoming heavily sedated. Its calming body character may appeal to people dealing with everyday muscular tension, minor aches, or physical discomfort, while the brighter early phase could be preferable for individuals who dislike cannabis varieties that feel mentally dull from the beginning.

Stress is another reason some consumers may gravitate toward this type of hybrid. A pleasant mood shift followed by gradually deepening relaxation can make the experience suitable for decompressing after demanding days. Appetite stimulation may also become noticeable as the effects mature, particularly at higher THC doses. Later in the evening, stronger amounts could encourage rest in people who find physical relaxation helpful before bedtime.

These potential applications should not be interpreted as evidence that Royal Cake treats any specific medical condition. Cannabis responses vary substantially among individuals, and the chemical composition of flower sold under the same strain name can differ between harvests. Anyone considering marijuana for persistent pain, anxiety, insomnia, or another diagnosed condition should discuss appropriate products and dosing with a qualified healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Breaking apart a well-cured flower reveals why this cultivar stands apart from more conventional Cake hybrids. Sweet cherry and ripe berry can arrive first, followed by a brighter citrus character that may resemble orange peel, tangerine candy, or tropical fruit. Beneath the fruit sits a smoother layer of cream, sherbet, vanilla, and lightly doughy sweetness. Some phenotypes push strongly toward candy and cherry, whereas Sherb-leaning plants can smell softer, creamier, and slightly more floral.

Caryophyllene is a logical contributor to the spicy, earthy foundation, while limonene complements the orange and citrus characteristics associated with the Tropicana-heavy side of the family. Myrcene can deepen the profile with herbal and musky fruit tones, and smaller amounts of linalool or pinene may introduce floral or fresh accents. Terpene dominance can change between phenotypes, so laboratory results should always take precedence over a generalized strain profile.

The flavor typically becomes more complex than the aroma alone suggests. Sweet berry and citrus can dominate the first impression before creamy sherbet develops through the middle of the palate. The finish may introduce pepper, earth, faint dough, or subtle gas that prevents the strain from tasting purely sugary. Proper curing is especially important with this type of weed because overly dry flower quickly loses the volatile citrus and cherry notes that give the cultivar much of its personality.
Growing Information

Grow More Fire gives Royal Cake a flowering period of approximately 60 days, placing most indoor plants comfortably within an eight- to nine-week window. Vegetative growth should show enough vigor to support topping, low-stress training, or a Screen of Green setup, although growers should evaluate individual plants before aggressively shaping them. Its hybrid structure is likely to produce moderate stretch after the light cycle changes, followed by increasingly dense floral clusters and substantial trichome development during the final weeks.

Color can become one of the garden’s standout traits. The breeder specifically notes the potential for attractive coloration, while the Super Buff Cherry side is associated with dark purple and highly resinous flowers. Cooler nighttime temperatures late in bloom may enhance genetically predisposed purple or reddish pigmentation, but excessive cold should never be used merely to force color. Bud density also means humidity deserves close attention. Strong circulation through the canopy and controlled late-flower moisture levels reduce the risk of mold becoming established inside tightly packed colas.

Official Royal Cake yield figures have not been published by Grow More Fire, so numbers presented for this cultivar should be treated as realistic estimates rather than breeder guarantees. A productive indoor garden can reasonably target roughly 450–550 g/m², while healthy outdoor plants given abundant root space, sunlight, nutrition, and a sufficiently long season may reach approximately 500–700 g each. Outdoor gardeners in the Northern Hemisphere should generally expect maturation around late September or early October, although latitude and phenotype can move that date in either direction.
FAQ
Is Royal Cake indica or sativa?
Grow More Fire Genetics classifies its version as a 50/50 hybrid, so it is neither strongly indica nor strongly sativa dominant.
What are the genetics of Royal Cake?

The authentic Grow More Fire version crosses Sherb Cake with Super Buff Cherry #26. The breeder identifies its Sherb Cake parent as Girl Scout Cookies × Pink Panties, while Super Buff Cherry #26 combines a Blockberry/Super Boof selection with Tropicana Cherry.
How strong is Royal Cake?

No official THC range is published by the breeder. Based on the potency of its parent lines and comparable flower, well-grown examples can reasonably fall within the low-to-upper 20% THC range, but a laboratory label is the only reliable way to know the strength of a particular batch.
What does Royal Cake taste like?

Expect a combination of cherry, sweet berries, citrus, creamy sherbet, vanilla-like sweetness, spice, and occasional earthy or gassy undertones. Individual plants may lean more toward fruit or toward the creamy Sherb side of the pedigree.
How long does Royal Cake take to flower?
The breeder specifies approximately 60 days of flowering, which translates to roughly eight to nine weeks for most indoor gardens.
Final Thoughts on Royal Cake

Royal Cake demonstrates how far modern Cake genetics have moved beyond simple vanilla-and-dough flavor profiles. Grow More Fire Genetics built the cultivar from Sherb Cake and the breeder’s own Super Buff Cherry #26 keeper, creating a balanced hybrid packed with Cookies, cherry, citrus, Tropicana, and dessert influences. Its appeal lies in that combination: colorful resinous flowers, lively fruit aromas, creamy sweetness, and effects that can transition smoothly from upbeat mental relaxation into a deeper physical calm.

For cannabis enthusiasts searching for a modern dessert strain that does not taste like another variation of Wedding Cake, this cultivar offers a noticeably different direction. Growers gain a relatively manageable 60-day flowering schedule and considerable phenotype-hunting potential, while consumers get a terpene profile capable of moving from orange-cherry candy to creamy sherbet and spice. Royal Cake is ultimately best understood not as a generic “Cake” weed strain, but as a distinct Grow More Fire creation whose Super Buff Cherry heritage gives the familiar dessert category a brighter, fruitier personality.
